UX review · branch ux-review · 17 Nov 2026

Tutorial Studio UX review.

This review covers every screen and component in apps/desktop: Projects, Brief, Demo capture, Storyboard, Live, Studio, Agent fix review, Export, Settings, Guide and the packages/ui kit. It is based on a full read of the source and on screenshots of the running app, then judged against one question: how would a new team member make and edit a tutorial?

~16,600 lines of UI read11 real-app screenshots and 3 fresh capturesSeverity: P0 blocker · P1 major · P2 minor · P3 polish

Verdict. The tool does powerful things, but it shows the user how it is built rather than what they are trying to do. Pipeline stages, takes, segments, sessions, skills, git commits, component IDs, codec names and costs per turn are all on screen. One idea often has three or four names. A newcomer has to learn about 70 concepts before an edit feels safe. The fix is mostly about removing and renaming things, not adding features. Three screens, one review point and one place to ask the agent would cover most of what people need.

5–6 → 3screens between "new tutorial" and a watchable video
17 → 1controls on the Brief; only the goal is required
~75 → ~30controls visible in the Studio before you select anything
14 → 4buttons in the timeline toolbar (the mockup had 4)

~70 → ~10concepts the in-app Guide has to teach
First principles

What a person actually comes here to do.

Strip away the machinery and the tool has two jobs. Each should feel like one obvious path.

1 · Make a tutorial

  • Say what the viewer should learn, and in which product.
  • Wait without worrying: see progress, get told when needed.
  • Check the script once, then approve.
  • Land in the editor when the video is ready.

2 · Polish and ship it

  • Watch it.
  • Fix what the narrator says in a step.
  • Cut or speed up a dull stretch.
  • Point at something: add an arrow or callout, or ask the agent.
  • Export and find the file.

What gets in the way today

  • Every system concept is a visible control.
  • The same thing has different names on different screens.
  • Things that need you are hidden in tabs or never announced.
  • Heavy actions (re-record, re-voice) are one unconfirmed click away.
  • Developer tools sit in the product UI.

Priorities

Fix these first.

  1. Show agent permission requests everywhere. In the Studio, "needs your approval" only appears inside the Agent tab, so a request sent from anywhere else stalls without any sign. ST-01
  2. Tell people when they're needed or done. Add OS notifications and a Dock badge for review points, failures and completion, and hand off to the Studio when the video is ready. X-04 · L-03
  3. One name per idea. Adopt the glossary below and rename across the UI, engine strings and Guide. The review step alone has four names today. X-01 · X-02
  4. Hide the machinery. Put cost, sessions, tool calls, diffs, IDs, codecs and the "Raw" console behind a Details toggle. Remove the dev shell, the pnpm engine chip and the "step 5.5" tooltip from production. X-05 · L-02 · ST-28 · A-02
  5. Confirm or offer undo for heavy actions: Regenerate VO (paid, and it re-times the video), Run again, Start again, Stop take, discarding a demo, and the single X key that inserts an explainer. X-07 · ST-12 · ST-15
  6. Collapse the start into one screen. Goal plus Make tutorial, with "Customize…" for the rest. Show the time and cost estimate the mockup already had. H-02 · B-01 · B-08
  7. Make the Studio about editing. Add a Script panel (step, narration text, re-voice), one inspector, three lanes, a 4-button toolbar and an always-visible "Ask the agent" box. Move the Pipeline and Skills tabs out. ST-02…ST-21
  8. Say where Export saves files and lead with "2:41 · 1080p · ~240 MB" rather than codec names. E-01 · E-03
  9. Make first-run setup safe and copyable: a default cost cap, copy buttons for Terminal commands, and the checklist above the create form. SE-01 · SE-02 · H-01
  10. Fix the fit at 1440×900. The timeline dock covers the bottom of the side panels, the preview gets about a third of the width, and the tool rail covers the video. ST-03 · ST-11
Root causes

Five patterns behind most findings.

The architecture is the UI

Each engine concept (stage, gate, take, segment, session, skill, commit, component) became a visible control or label. Users see the system's model, not their task.

Names drift

Features were added step by step and each got its own word. The same idea ends up as narration, VO, voice line and line, or gate, review, plan review and storyboard review.

State hides

Requests, errors and "needs you" signals sit in tabs, tooltips and chips that never clear. The Studio reports status in 7 places, yet the one that matters (a permission request) is in none of them.

Everything weighs the same

Batch operations sit beside Split and Undo. Re-record is as prominent as Export. Seventeen brief options all look equally important. Without hierarchy, users can't tell what's primary.

No shared primitives

There's no Toast, ConfirmDialog, Popover, Notice, Tooltip or type scale in the kit. Each screen invents its own, which gives 8 error-message styles, 247 inline styles, 18 font sizes and 12 radii.

Terminology

One word per idea.

Rename everywhere: UI, engine messages, gate titles and the Guide. Keep internal names in code if needed, but never on screen.

Proposal

A Studio built around editing.

Production (stages, review points, what the agent learned, runs) leaves the editor and comes back as notifications. The editor keeps what a person edits: the video, the script, the overlays and one way to ask for help.

Fix plan

Four phases, smallest risk first.

Phase A · quick wins

Stop the bleeding

  • Mount permission requests in the Studio and Live; add a needs-you dot
  • OS notifications and an "Open in the Studio" hand-off
  • Confirm or undo toasts on heavy actions; remove the bare X shortcut
  • Hide the dev shell, the engine chip, IDs, cost and the step-5.5 tooltip
  • Fix "Approved.", Live's "Try again" labels and the Export save path
ST-01 X-04 L-01 L-03 X-05 X-07 S-01 E-01
Phase B · words

One vocabulary

  • Apply the glossary across the UI, engine strings and gate titles
  • Rewrite jargon copy (timing, late cues, auto mode, export)
  • Cut the Guide to the happy path and move "How it's built" to docs
X-01 X-02 B-03 ST-19 G-01 G-03
Phase C · structure

Fewer screens, clearer Studio

  • Home starts the run, with the Brief behind Customize…
  • Merge Storyboard and Live into "Making your tutorial"
  • Studio: Script panel, one inspector, 3 lanes, + Add menu, agent box
  • Move the Pipeline and Skills tabs out of the Studio
H-02 B-01 S-07 L-04 ST-02…ST-27
Phase D · kit

Make it stay fixed

  • Add Toast, ConfirmDialog, Popover, Notice, Tooltip, Kbd and Checkbox to packages/ui
  • Type, space and radius tokens; a lint rule against raw px and hex
  • Primary-button contrast, focus rings, keyboard timeline
D-01…D-12
Keep these

What already works.

  • The home hero and suggestion chips make the starting point clear.
  • Export matches its mockup closely, and choosing outputs is simple.
  • The ElevenLabs key is handled well: it's checked before saving, kept in the Keychain and never shown again.
  • Icon buttons and tool-rail tools have aria-label and aria-keyshortcuts; the scrubber is a real slider; reduced motion is respected.
  • Theme switching keeps the video light, as the design rules require.
  • Undo and redo exist for every timeline patch. They just need to say what they'll undo.
